published_final_diagnosis.label: Malignant chylothorax as initial manifestation of extensive-stage small cell lung carcinoma

source_treatment.description: Indwelling pleural catheter for recurrent symptomatic effusion

source_disposition.outcome: Partial response, then pneumonia, Pseudomonas bacteremia, septic shock and death.

key_guideline_decisions.note: See docs/guideline_sources.yaml; applicability and alternative care require clinician review.

distractors: Negative initial pleural cytology; lymphoma is a more common malignant cause of chylothorax.
critical_safety_points: Symptomatic recurrent pleural effusion needs drainage and assessment of cause.
Negative pleural cytology does not rule out thoracic malignancy.
Long-term chyle drainage raises nutritional and immune concerns.

source_locators: PDF p. 1, second ED visit and repeat thoracentesis
PDF p. 1, initial thoracentesis and Table 1

source_uncertainties: Unspecified dose, timing or normal findings were not inferred.
Published management is descriptive and requires separate normative review.
The acute ED return is the benchmark time zero. Initial thoracentesis and its fluid studies are prior records; the article does not document a specific inpatient ward disposition for this return.
